South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and ongoing management of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment one month after his last visit. He reports that while his dyspnea remains stable, he has noted an increase in the frequency of his albuterol inhaler use to five to six times daily, particularly during episodes of increased physical activity. He remains compliant with his inhaled corticosteroids and continues to attend pulmonary rehabilitation sessions, expressing that the structured exercise has been beneficial for his lung function and overall stamina.
The bilateral lower extremity edema continues to be a concern, with Mr. Fairfax reporting no significant change despite adherence to a low-sodium diet and furosemide therapy at 100 mg daily. He describes the edema as 1+ pitting, unchanged from last month, and continues to practice leg elevation without notable improvement. He denies any new symptoms such as shortness of breath or chest pain associated with the edema.
Mr. Fairfax reports persistent fatigue that he describes as overwhelming, impacting his daily activities. He acknowledges slight improvements in his mood attributed to ongoing therapy sessions, yet he continues to experience episodes of anxiety. He is compliant with his sertraline regimen, which he feels has provided some relief from his depressive symptoms, although he expresses a desire for further improvement.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using five to six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 78, BP 130/80, RR 18, O2 sat 89% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress, appears fatigued but alert. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.0, Hgb 10.4, Hct 31.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 133, K 4.0, Cl 98, CO2 24, BUN 30, Cr 1.5, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 590 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status remains stable, although increased inhaler use is noted. It is recommended he continue with pulmonary rehabilitation and strict adherence to inhaled corticosteroids. A follow-up appointment in 1 month is warranted for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema continues to be managed with furosemide. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended to evaluate renal function further due to the increase in creatinine. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Mr. Fairfax has reported minor improvements in anxiety and depressive symptoms, and ongoing psychological support is encouraged. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
